To add to that, why won't anymore be built? Is there a new design? And I bet it does move around, but what do I know?

The Iowa class battleships are what is meant by classic. The biggest things that stick out about this ship design are the wooden weather decks, and the 16 inch guns (the gun bore is 16 inches, not the length). Other examples of this design are the USS Wisconsin, or the USS New Jersey.

The reason that more battleships won't be built is because an aircraft carrier has a range of hundreds of miles, whereas a battleship has a range of a couple of miles. If you put a strike group (a couple of cruisers, destroyers, and a sub or two) around an aircraft carrier then these ships acting in concert have much better defense than a battleship does.

Basically what happened is everyone started building bigger and bigger battleships in WW1, and in the lead up to WW2, expecting that the naval battles would be won by the ships with the biggest guns and armor. The Yamamoto class of Japanese battleships are really impressive, with the largest naval guns ever used (19 inch guns). When Pearl Harbor was attacked it showed decisively that air power was superior to battleships, and the United States has decided that a carrier strike group is the best way to go.

source: I was a Fire Controlman in the US Navy. A Fire Controlman is the guy who gets to shoot and maintain the artillery and missiles (Some Gunners Mates may take issue with this, as they do the maintenance on a lot of the systems as well).
I visited the USS New Jersey and read that these larger cannons can shoot 5ft tall projectiles 27 miles!
